delivered: Mitigation proposal: Establish a closed-loop “screw-recovery/weight drift” control using only existing sensors (barrel thermocouples, cycle-time logger, and check-weigher). Mechanism: Treat the increasing screw recovery time and part weight drift as an indicator of degraded melt density/consistency and inconsistent back-off behavior; use the check-weigher output at the quality gate and the cycle-time logger’s recovery-time trend to detect drift, and automatically adjust the injection hold time/pressure setpoint and/or back-off speed to bring part weight back to target within the same barrel setpoints. DIRECTION-OF-EFFECT: Decreasing the back-off speed increases the metering volume and mass of material fed into the barrel, which drives the part weight upward. Increasing the injection hold pressure increases the residual packing mass injected into the cavity during the hold phase, which drives the part weight upward. Implementation: 1) From the check-weigher, compute rolling average part weight and deviation from target; 2) From the cycle-time logger, compute rolling average screw recovery time and detect increases beyond a threshold; 3) When both conditions persist for a defined window, trigger a corrective action: reduce the back-off speed (to ensure more complete metering) and/or increase injection hold pressure slightly to stabilize density, while keeping barrel temperature setpoints unchanged; 4) Log the adjustments and verify with subsequent check-weigher readings that weight returns to target and recovery time stabilizes. Measures relied on: Existing sensors only—barrel thermocouples (to confirm no temperature drift is causing the issue), cycle-time logger (for recovery time monitoring), and check-weigher (for part weight feedback). No new instrumentation is added; the mitigation uses data fusion from these existing measurements to implement a simple feedback correction to process parameters (back-off speed/hold pressure) that affects part weight and screw recovery consistency. IMPLEMENTATION BILL: 1. Control System Input Mapping: Part weight error = (Check-weigher raw mass reading - Target Part Weight) [Source: Check-weigher]. Recovery time trend = (Rolling Average of Screw Recovery Time - Baseline Recovery Time) [Source: Cycle-time logger]. Thermal Status Flag = (Max Barrel Zone Temperature - Target Barrel Zone Temperature) [Source: Barrel zone thermocouples]. 2. Decision Logic: IF |Part weight error| > Threshold_Weight AND (Recovery time trend > Threshold_Recovery) AND Thermal Status Flag within normal range THEN Execute Correction. 3. Actuator Commands: If Part weight error is negative (part too light), Command: Increase Back-off Speed or Increase Injection Hold Pressure. If Part weight error is positive (part too heavy), Command: Decrease Back-off Speed or Decrease Injection Hold Pressure. 4. Verification Loop: Read subsequent Check-weigher outputs and Cycle-time logger recovery times to confirm convergence.
